newsitem.title: USA: CBOT soybeans close lower as wheat tumbles.
newsitem.headline: CBOT soybeans close lower as wheat tumbles.

text.p: CBOT soybean futures closed weaker on Thursday, in line with a late slide in wheat futures, with commercial and commission house selling noted, traders said.
"Beans traded off of wheat. When wheat broke beans broke," said Ron Kucha of O'Connor and Co. "It wasn't that big a volume day, the markets just bounced around."
Soybeans had opened lower on a technical correction following two days of strong gains but commercial buying in the soyoil pit fueled rumors China was buying soy products, traders said.
ADM Investor Services was said to be a buyer which prompted fund buying and stops were hit, traders said.

On the day, Refco Inc sold 3.5 million bushels January while Merrill Lynch Futures sold 3 million bushels March, traders said. Cargill Inc sold one million bushels January while Continental Grain was said to be a buyer.
In options trading, Cargill Investor Services bought at least 700 January $7.25 calls at 3-1/2 cents, traders said. Refco Inc sold at least 200 January $6.75 calls at 21 cents.
Soybeans ended 2-1/4 to 3/4 cents per bushel lower with January down 2-1/4 at $6.88-1/4.
Volume was estimated at 45,000 contracts, compared with Wednesday's volume of 58,436.
